devon: Heads up — CI red on rate_limiter_timer_test on linux-20 and arm64-nightly. Failing ~1/5 runs.
carla: Ugh. Any flaky log paste?
devon: Pasted snippet from the failing run:
```\nASSERT: expected token_count == 0 but got 1\n#0 0x7f... in Timer::on_timeout()\n#1 0x7f... in RateLimiter::maybe_release()\n...\n``` 
alice: Looks like timer firing after latch release? Could be scheduler ordering or clock drift.
ben: Is this happening after the retry backoff refactor from last week?
devon: Possibly — last green was 9cf4a7b. CI shows new ordering in RateLimiter::try_acquire -> schedule timer -> release path.
carla: Can someone bisect the reg quickly? I can try but need to repro locally first
eva: I can run stress in docker with --repeat 200 locally and try the arm64 image cross-runner
ci-bot: re-run job #4523 requested by carla — queued
devon: Quick test: add a short sleep in the timer handler and see if failure disappears. If so, points to a race with immediate wake.
alice: Also try setting CLOCK_MONOTONIC_COARSE vs MONOTONIC — kernel timers vary.
ben: If we can't easily repro, suggest adding an assertion guard to log the ownership/epoch to help bisect without changing timing.
carla: I'll add extra debug logging behind a flag and push a short patch to the flaky tests CI branch.
eva: While that's running, bumping the test's retry count to 3 might reduce noise in CI.
devon: If someone can run `./scripts/ci_rerun.sh --job rate_limiter_timer_test --repeat 100 --env DEBUG_TIMER=1` that'd help.
carla: Kicked off a bisect job against 9cf4a7b..HEAD — I'll post updates, thanks.
ci-bot: Job #4524 finished: still failing (3/50). Attached log: https://ci.internal/runs/4524
alice: On-call note: if we see >10% failure rate across matrix, escalate to infra to run under perf-capture.
ben: FYI I saw a similar pattern in preemptive-scheduler branch — maybe the timer callback can be invoked concurrently during shutdown path
devo n: (typo) — devon: good catch, ben. I'll check the shutdown sequence with timers held.
carla: Thanks all — will circle back after bisect results. :eyes:
